column1: # Cron vectors derived from cron-utils's ExecutionTimeUnixIntegrationTest
column2: its Issue* regression tests and its parser tests

column9: src/test/java/com/cronutils/Issue228Test.java

column1: # licence: Apache-2.0 (Copyright 2015 jmrozanec). Each row restates one assertion of the named tests as an expression
column3: attributed by test name and line; no upstream file is copied.

column1: # method: transcribed by hand from the named tests
# note: cron-utils parses per definition. UNIX rows (five fields
column3: N/step to the field maximum) apply as written
column4: but UNIX unions the day fields unless one is exactly * (so */n is restricted there and unrestricted in Bodu). QUARTZ (seconds first
column7: ? in one day field) and SPRING (seconds first
column8: weekday 0-7) rows are restated with weekday names for Quartz numbers and a * year dropped; definitions with ? (QUARTZ
column9: SPRING
column10: custom matchDayOfWeekAndDayOfMonth) intersect two restricted day fields
column11: so those rows are cronsim restatements under the Vixie union. isMatch is restated as next-inclusive (previous-inclusive below a second) and timeFromLastExecution as previous. Left out: 49 test methods - 10 that depend on a named zone's transitions (DST)

column1: # flags: year-field = the row depends on a year field
# flags: wrap-range = a reversed range the library wraps; Bodu rejects it
# flags: oversized-step = a step wider than its range the library rejects; Bodu takes the range start
# flags: quartz-dow-numbering = Quartz 1=Sunday weekday digits that cannot be renumbered without changing the row's meaning
# flags: token-list = Quartz tokens inside lists
# flags: syntax-extension = library-only syntax (a day-of-year field
# flags: question-mark = the QUARTZ definition requires ? in one day field; Bodu reads ? as * and does not require it
